column4: To use this phrase, you need an action first. Most commonly, you'll hear it with the verb 'do' - *'do something by the book'*, or *'do things by the book'*.
column5: So, to remember it, maybe imagine a book of rules that you follow, but it doesn't have to be a physical book of rules. | Example:✦ I know when some people are cooking, they just, like, throw any old ingredients in there and make it up as they go along, but 3*I like to do it by the book* and follow the recipe.
column6: 3*I do everything by the book* and it does make it slower, which can be a bit annoying, but, yeah, got to follow the rules.
column7: Our accountant is very thorough. 3*He does everything by the book*, so I trust his judgement.

I've just had a little mooch around the shops in my lunch break, and now I'm ready to get back to work.
column4: So, 'mooch' or 'mooch around' is an informal British English word or phrase which means to wander or stroll around casually.
column5: We use it when we're exploring shops, markets or streets without the aim of reaching a specific destination.
column6: If we want to specify where to mooch, we add 'around', like when you said you 3*"had a little mooch around the shops*".
column7: You don't always need the verb 'have' – mooch can act as a verb itself, for example '"I *mooched around* the shops in my lunchbreak". | Example:✦ I really need some caffeine. I'm just going to *mooch around* the centre until I find a cafe.
column8: We landed at 9 o'clock at night, so there wasn't really anything to do, apart from *mooch around* the night market.
column9: There's a new art gallery that's opened up in town, I, I don't know a lot about it, but I'm, I'm just going to go and *have a mooch* and see what's there. | Notes:✦ You can use the set phrase 4*'have a mooch'* in a similar way that we use 4*'have a look'*. You can say 4*"Let's have a mooch"* if you want to invite someone to wander aimlessly somewhere, without specifying the location.
column10: We've learnt the word *'mooch'* which means 5*stroll around casually, often without purpose.*
column11: Now I really want to 5*mooch around the city* at the weekend. It sounds very relaxing!
